title_original: Book of Negroes
description: Nova Scotia Archives' online presentation of the British copy of the 1783 Book of Negroes, a register of about 3,000 Black refugees who sailed from New York to Nova Scotia between April and November 1783. You can page through digitized images of the register, which is held in the UK.
content_note: Title uses historical terminology now considered offensive; retained as written by the source.
container_title: African Nova Scotians in the Age of Slavery and Abolition
notes: NSA says two originals were made at the same time. The British one (shown here) is at The National Archives, Kew. The American one is at the US National Archives in Washington, and NSA holds microfilm of it (nos. 23164 and 23165). The page also explains historical place names (St. Johns = Saint John NB; Port Roseway = Shelburne; Fort Cumberland near Amherst).
holder_note: The NSA landing page says the British version is in the "Sir Guy Carlton papers at the Public Records Office" (spelled Carlton there), reference PRO 30/55/100. Equating the Public Records Office with today's The National Archives (Kew) is our identification. Every image page is captioned "Guy Carleton, 1st Baron Dorchester: Papers, The National Archives, Kew (PRO 30/55/100)" (spelled Carleton). TNA's own story page uses the same reference and points to Discovery C3070438, which could not be rendered.
access_instructions: Page through the register images with the previous/next links from the landing page. The original is at The National Archives, Kew (PRO 30/55/100).
rights_statement: Page contents are Crown copyright, Province of Nova Scotia. Personal, non-commercial use of web images is allowed. Commercial, educational or media use needs a Rights Declaration and an Image Use Request to NSA. Credit the Nova Scotia Archives.
change_notes: Split from SRC-001 (v1), which had merged the NSA and LAC descriptions. The v1 title "Book of Negroes, 1783" is LAC's form; NSA labels it "Book of Negroes". v1 reference "Guy Carleton papers, PRO 30/55/100" is now source_reference "PRO 30/55/100". CONFLICT (kept NSA's range): date ranges differ across sources. NSA gives 23 April–30 November 1783, LAC gives April–November 1783, and TNA gives 15 April 1783–19 February 1784 (the TNA range includes later board hearings and a London signing). The date_display wording comes from a WebFetch summary; check it by eye.

title_original: Book of Negroes, 1783
description: Library and Archives Canada's searchable name index of the British copy of the 1783 Book of Negroes. It covers about 3,000 Black men, women and children who left New York for Nova Scotia, searchable by details such as age, gender, place of origin and ship.
content_note: Title uses historical terminology now considered offensive; retained as written by the source. LAC also gives a historical language advisory: some racial descriptors in the register entries are considered offensive today.
notes: LAC calls the Book of Negroes a small part of the British Headquarters Papers. It presents the database under "Carleton Papers - Loyalists and British Soldiers, 1772 to 1784". The database is a transcription made from microfilm of the British version, not page images. About 800 entries have no surname. LAC says the American version is at the US National Archives and Records Administration.
holder_note: LAC's page says the British version is held at the UK National Archives as part of the Carleton Papers. It gives no TNA reference number. PRO 30/55/100 comes from the NSA and TNA pages (see SRC-001a).
access_instructions: Search LAC's transcribed database with the "Search the Book of Negroes, 1783" link on the page. The advanced keyword field accepts age, gender, place of origin or ship. To see the record itself, view the microfilm in person at LAC in Ottawa, order copies, or hire a researcher. Page images of the British original are on the Nova Scotia Archives site.
rights_statement: Government of Canada material. Accurate, credited non-commercial reproduction needs no permission. Commercial redistribution needs written permission from LAC.
change_notes: Split from SRC-001 (v1). The LAC page shows no PRO/MG reference or reel number, so PRO 30/55/100 was not carried here. Page date modified 2026-10-01. The search database URL was not visible in the fetched content. CONFLICT (kept LAC's wording): the Book of Negroes date range differs across NSA, LAC and TNA (see SRC-001a). content_note: The source page quotes period official language that describes Black refugees in demeaning terms. It is not reproduced here.

title_original: Loyalists
description: Library and Archives Canada's research guide to Loyalist records (military, Loyalist lists, land and settlement, published sources). It includes pointers for Black Loyalist research such as the Book of Negroes and the 1784 Birchtown muster book.
content_note: The page carries LAC's historical language advisory: older records may use language about Black Canadians now considered offensive.
notes: A broad Loyalist guide, not a Black-history-only resource. It links to LAC's Book of Negroes, 1783 page, a "Black Loyalist refugees, 1782 to 1807" (Port Roseway Associates) page, and the Black Canadians guide. title_original: Portia May White (1911-1968) National Historic Person

title_original: John Ware (circa 1850–1905) National Historic Person

notes: Designated 2022. The page says his early life is unclear and that he was likely enslaved in the American South. Married Mildred Lewis in 1892; both died in 1905. Plaque at Bar U Ranch National Historic Site, Longview, Alberta. Photos are credited to University of Calgary collections.

title_original: Harriet Tubman (circa 1822-1913) National Historic Person

title_original: Charlow (Shiloh) Baptist Church and Cemetery
description: Saskatchewan heritage-property record for the log church built in 1912 by Black settlers who came from Oklahoma in 1910, and for the cemetery beside it. It explains why the site is significant and lists the features that protect its heritage character.
notes: Resource kind: heritage designation record. The document heading reads "Heritage Property - Charlow (Shiloh) Baptist Church and Cemetery". It records a Municipal Heritage Property designated December 4, 1991 under Rural Municipality of Eldon No. 471 Bylaw No. 114, about 30 km north of Maidstone. About 12 founding families grew to over fifty; the church was used until the mid-1940s and the cemetery (an estimated 37 graves) from 1913 to 1945. The site is also on the Canadian Register of Historic Places (https://www.historicplaces.ca/en/rep-reg/place-lieu.aspx?id=4207; Register ID 4207; FPT identifier MHP 439; listed January 16, 2006), not used as source_url because the National Trust for Canada reported on 2026-01-19 that the database would be "permanently unplugged in spring 2026".
holder_note: Designation record for a built heritage site, not an archival item. CRHP says the supporting documentation is in Heritage Resources Branch file MHP 439.
source_reference: 174 (document number in the Heritage Property Search URL)
access_instructions: Free PDF online. The site itself is in the Rural Municipality of Eldon No. 471, about 30 km north of Maidstone, Saskatchewan.

title_original: Robert Lawson and 11 Others (Front)
description: Image and transcription of a 1785 land petition, labelled "Blacks of Maugerville", from Robert Lawson and eleven other Black men in Maugerville, New Brunswick, addressed to Thomas Carleton. It appears in the Fredericton Region Museum's online exhibit on early Black settlers of York-Sunbury counties; the original is credited to the Provincial Archives of New Brunswick.
container_title: Our Black Heritage: Early Black Settlers of York-Sunbury Counties (New Brunswick) 1783-Present
notes: The museum caption dates the petition 1785, and the credit line also gives 1785. The transcription on the same page is dated "Feb 25, 1784". The page does not explain the difference; both dates are recorded. The exhibit is hosted on Community Stories (Digital Museums Canada). The museum's announcement says it opened at the Fredericton Region Museum on August 1, 2021, with PANB, UNB, Kings Landing, the New Brunswick Museum and community groups as partners. Petitioners' names are entered exactly as transcribed by the museum. "(Front)" suggests a back side or second page exists; not checked.
holder_note: The page credit line reads "Courtesy of Provincial Archives of New Brunswick, F1027, 1785." The source (the museum's exhibit page) and the holder (PANB) are different institutions.
